Terminaison présynaptique de notre axone: Presynaptic terminal of our axon: ≈ 200 synaptic vesicles, about ten of them docked at the active zone, facing the spine of a neighbouring neuron. Enter it through the clathrin-coated pit, or approach the cleft from outside: the ship shrinks until it can slip in. Every molecule of the synapse has its own card. The ⚡ button lets you follow a nerve impulse from end to end.
Tête de ≈ 0,5 µm portée par un col étroi: A head of ≈ 0.5 µm on a narrow neck; its membrane hugs our bouton at a distance of 20 nm. Beneath that membrane lies the postsynaptic density: AMPA and NMDA receptors, then the layered scaffold of PSD-95, GKAP, Shank and Homer, linked to actin. Inserting or removing AMPA receptors underlies long-term potentiation and depression.
Une des ≈ 10 000 épines de notre neurone: One of the ≈ 10,000 spines of our neuron, with its excitatory synapse. Its narrow neck (≈ 0.1 to 0.2 µm) makes it a biochemical compartment: Ca²⁺ entering through NMDA receptors stays confined there, which makes plasticity specific to each synapse. This is where the ⚡ nerve-impulse tour begins.
Renflement « en passant » d'un axone ven: An “en passant” swelling of an axon coming from another neuron. A hippocampal bouton has on average one active zone of ≈ 0.04 µm², about ten docked vesicles and ≈ 200 vesicles in all (Schikorski and Stevens 1997). An action potential releases a vesicle there only with a certain probability.
Collatérale fine et sans myéline d'un ne: A thin, unmyelinated collateral of an upstream neuron. It forms an “en passant” bouton every few micrometres and so contacts thousands of neurons.
≈ 20 nm séparent les deux membranes, soi: ≈ 20 nm separate the two membranes, about five membrane thicknesses. The cleft is spanned by adhesion molecules (neurexins, neuroligins, cadherins) that keep the two sides aligned. Released glutamate reaches ≈ 1 mM there and is gone within ≈ 1 ms (Clements 1992): diffusion, then uptake by astrocyte transporters.
Trimère de la membrane astrocytaire (gèn: A trimer of the astrocyte membrane (gene SLC1A2), present in thousands of copies per µm². It brings in one glutamate with 3 Na⁺ and 1 H⁺ and exports 1 K⁺: enough to keep extracellular glutamate below one micromolar. In the astrocyte, glutamine synthetase converts glutamate into glutamine (the glutamate–glutamine cycle).
Vésicule de ≈ 40 nm retenue contre la zo: A ≈ 40 nm vesicle held against the active zone, its SNARE complexes half zippered: it is ready to fuse as soon as Ca²⁺ arrives. An active zone holds about ten of them (the readily releasable pool). Docking and priming depend on RIM, Munc13-1 and Munc18-1.
Faisceau de quatre hélices long de ≈ 12: A bundle of four helices ≈ 12 nm long: syntaxin-1 and SNAP-25 (two helices) on the plasma membrane, synaptobrevin-2 (VAMP2) on the vesicle. Its zippering, from the N-terminal end towards the membranes, forces them together and supplies the energy for fusion. NSF and α-SNAP then take it apart using ATP. Botulinum and tetanus toxins are proteases that cleave these three proteins.
Petite hélice fixée dans le sillon du co: A small helix lodged in the groove of the half-zippered SNARE complex. It stabilises the complex while holding fusion back; Ca²⁺-bound synaptotagmin releases this brake.

Anchored in the vesicle, it carries two C2 domains (C2A binds 3 Ca²⁺, C2B binds 2) which, once loaded, plunge into the phospholipids of the plasma membrane and trigger fusion in less than a millisecond. Its low affinity (tens of µM) restricts fusion to vesicles sitting right next to an open calcium channel.
A protein of the SM family (gene STXBP1). It holds syntaxin-1 folded, then guides assembly of the SNARE complex; without it there is no neurotransmitter release. STXBP1 variants cause a developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.

Opened by the action potential, it creates around itself a nanodomain where Ca²⁺ reaches tens of µM for less than a millisecond. Release varies as roughly the 4th power of Ca²⁺.

A few tens to about a hundred per synapse; their number sets the strength of the synapse.

Slow and highly permeable to Ca²⁺, it detects the coincidence of pre- and postsynaptic activity and triggers plasticity. Variants of the GRIN genes cause neurodevelopmental disorders and epilepsies.

Variants of DLG4 and SYNGAP1 cause intellectual disability.

Échafaudage de la couche profonde (SHANK: Scaffold of the deep layer (SHANK1 to SHANK3). It binds GKAP, Homer and cortactin, and so links the receptors to the actin of the spine. Loss of one copy of SHANK3 (22q13.3 deletion) causes Phelan-McDermid syndrome.

Variants of CAMK2A and CAMK2B cause intellectual disability.

Empilement de citernes de réticulum liss: A stack of smooth reticulum cisternae, organised by synaptopodin, found in a minority of spines, the largest ones. A Ca²⁺ store and a relay for local protein trafficking.
Une seule chaîne (gène SCN8A) de quatre: A single chain (gene SCN8A) of four domains with six transmembrane segments each; the charged S4 segments are the voltage sensors. It opens in less than a millisecond, then inactivates by itself: the IFM motif of the III–IV loop plugs the pore (orange bead, cytosolic side). The Nav1.6 channels of the distal initial segment trigger the action potential; the proximal Nav1.2 (SCN2A) channels carry it back towards the soma (Hu 2009). Typical concentrations: K⁺ 140 mM inside, 4 mM outside; Na⁺ 12 mM inside, 145 mM outside; free Ca²⁺ 0.1 µM inside, 1.2 mM outside.

If the spine is strongly depolarised at the same moment — several synapses active together, or an action potential travelling back up the dendrite — the Mg²⁺ is expelled and Ca²⁺ (orange) enters. This Ca²⁺ activates CaMKII: the synapse will be strengthened.

It is slow (tens to hundreds of ms) and highly permeable to Ca²⁺. Ca²⁺/calmodulin activates CaMKII, whose autophosphorylation on Thr286 prolongs its activity; it binds GluN2B and promotes the addition of AMPA receptors to the postsynaptic density: this is long-term potentiation (Lisman 2012). The spine, isolated by its neck, confines this calcium signal to the active synapse.

One transport cycle takes tens of milliseconds; it is the sheer number of transporters (thousands per µm²) that traps glutamate quickly. In the astrocyte, glutamine synthetase converts it into glutamine (the glutamate–glutamine cycle). In the bouton, endocytosis (clathrin, dynamin; an ultrafast pathway also exists) regenerates vesicles, the V-ATPase acidifies them and VGLUT1 fills them. An EPSP of several millivolts in the spine is worth only a few tenths of a millivolt at the soma. Meanwhile, other synapses fire (flashes): their EPSPs add up.
La dendrite se comporte comme un câble :: The dendrite behaves like a cable: axial resistance, membrane resistance and membrane capacitance set a length constant (hundreds of µm) and a time constant (tens of ms) that filter the signal. Spatial summation: distinct synapses active together; temporal summation: one synapse active at high frequency. The dendrite is not merely passive: its HCN (Ih current), Kv4 and Nav channels shape integration, and distal synapses have a larger conductance, which partly offsets their distance (Magee 2000). On the order of tens to a hundred synapses must be active together to reach threshold.

Placed on the soma, just before the axon initial segment, it holds a veto. The oscilloscope shows stepwise summation, an inhibitory potential that delays it, then the crossing of threshold.

The action potential is all-or-none: its amplitude does not depend on the stimulus; information is carried by the rate and timing of firing. Each action potential moves only a tiny fraction of the ions: concentrations barely change.

The action potential also travels back towards the soma and dendrites: this backpropagation tells the synapses that the neuron has fired.

A hippocampal bouton has on average one active zone of ≈ 0.04 µm², about ten docked vesicles and ≈ 200 vesicles in all (Schikorski and Stevens 1997).

Un nucléosome peut porter plusieurs de c: A nucleosome can carry several of these marks, and it is their combination along the genome that defines the chromatin state. Active promoter: H3K4me3 and H3K27ac. Active enhancer: H3K4me1 and H3K27ac. Transcribed gene: H3K79me2 at the start, H3K36me3 further on. Polycomb: H3K27me3 and H2AK119ub1. Constitutive heterochromatin: H3K9me3, H4K20me3 and DNA methylation. The nucleosome shown here carries them all as a reminder: no real nucleosome does. All are reversible. When the genes of their writers, readers and erasers are altered, they cause Mendelian developmental disorders: the Mendelian genetics focus, on the start screen, lists them at each step.

Each step shows one chemical mark on a histone or on the DNA: the protein that writes it (blue-green), the one that reads it (violet), the one that erases it (ochre), and what it means for the gene. The marks have the colours used in chromatin-state maps. Drag to turn around the scene, use the wheel or pinch to zoom; “Contents” jumps straight to a mark. The positions of the tails and proteins are schematic.
Les marques ne suffisent pas : pour qu'u: Marks are not enough: for a factor to reach the DNA, the nucleosome often has to be moved. Remodellers are ATP-driven motors: here the BAF complex (SWI/SNF; motor BRG1, subunit ARID1B) slides the DNA over the octamer, one to two base pairs at a time (step measured in yeast; white marker). Others swap a histone for a variant: the SRCAP complex replaces an H2A–H2B dimer with an H2A.Z–H2B dimer.
Deux marques opposées sur un même nucléo: Two opposite marks on the same nucleosome: H3K4me3 on one H3 tail, H3K27me3 on the other. Described in embryonic stem cells, on the promoters of developmental genes, this “bivalent” state keeps the gene off but ready to start. The two marks sit on opposite tails: PRC2 is blocked when both H3 tails carry H3K4me3, not when only one does.
La marque portée par l'ADN lui-même : un: The mark carried by the DNA itself: a methyl on carbon 5 of a cytosine followed by a guanine (CpG). Writers: DNMT3A and DNMT3B lay it down; after each replication, UHRF1 spots the sites methylated on one strand only and DNMT1 copies the mark onto the new strand. Reader: MeCP2, which recruits histone deacetylases. Erasers: the TET enzymes, which oxidise the methyl step by step; the base is then replaced. Most CpGs in the genome are methylated; those in promoter CpG islands are not.
H2AX est un variant de H2A dont la queue: H2AX is a variant of H2A whose C-terminal tail carries serine 139. Within minutes of a double-strand break, the kinases ATM, ATR or DNA-PK phosphorylate it over megabases around the lesion: this is γH2AX. Reader: MDC1, through its BRCT domains; it gathers the repair machinery. Erasers: the phosphatases PP2A and PP4.
Un phosphate sur la sérine 10, voisine i: A phosphate on serine 10, right next to lysine 9. In mitosis, the kinase Aurora B phosphorylates S10 on all chromosomes: HP1, which was reading H3K9me3 next door, is ejected (methyl-phospho switch). Eraser: the phosphatase PP1. Outside mitosis, the same mark is written by MSK1 and MSK2 on the nucleosomes of immediate-early genes such as FOS, where it accompanies their activation.
Trois méthyles sur la lysine 9 de H3 : l: Three methyls on lysine 9 of H3: the mark of constitutive heterochromatin, which stays closed in every cell (pericentromeric regions, transposable elements). Writers: SUV39H1 and SUV39H2; SETDB1 on retroelements; G9a and GLP (EHMT2 and EHMT1) write H3K9me1 and me2, abundant against the lamina. Reader: HP1 (here HP1α, gene CBX5), through its chromodomain. Downstream of H3K9me3 and HP1, SUV420H1 and H2 trimethylate H4K20. Erasers: the KDM4 demethylases.
Une ubiquitine sur la lysine 119 de H2A,: A ubiquitin on lysine 119 of H2A, at the start of its C-terminal tail. Writers: RING1B (RNF2) or RING1A, in PRC1 complexes; at Polycomb targets it comes mostly from the so-called variant PRC1 complexes (RING1A or B, a PCGF protein, RYBP or YAF2). Reader: JARID2, a PRC2 subunit: the mark thus attracts PRC2 and links the two Polycomb systems. Eraser: BAP1, with ASXL1, 2 or 3 (PR-DUB complex).
Trois méthyles sur la lysine 27 de H3 :: Three methyls on lysine 27 of H3: the mark of facultative heterochromatin, that of genes switched off depending on the cell type (developmental genes, inactive X chromosome). Writer: the Polycomb complex PRC2, made of EZH2 (the catalytic subunit), EED and SUZ12. Readers: the chromodomain of CBX proteins of the PRC1 complex (here CBX2; not all of them prefer this mark); and EED itself, which stimulates PRC2 and spreads the mark step by step. Erasers: UTX (KDM6A) and KDM6B.
Une ubiquitine entière (76 acides aminés: A whole ubiquitin (76 amino acids) is attached to lysine 120 of H2B, on the surface of the nucleosome, during transcription. Writers: RNF20 and RNF40, with the enzyme UBE2A (RAD6). This mark triggers others: it stimulates DOT1L, which methylates lysine 79 in the globular domain of H3 (H3K79me2, at the start of transcribed genes), and COMPASS, which writes H3K4me3. Eraser: USP22, in the SAGA complex.
H2BK120ub1 et H3K79me2 : une marque en a: H2BK120ub1 and H3K79me2: one mark calls for another
Trois méthyles sur la lysine 36, à la ba: Three methyls on lysine 36, at the base of the H3 tail: the mark of transcribed gene bodies, denser toward their 3′ end. Writer: SETD2, which makes nearly all H3K36me3 and travels with RNA polymerase II, bound to its phosphorylated CTD tail. Reader: the PWWP domain of DNMT3B, which then methylates the DNA of the gene body; together, these two marks prevent transcription from starting in the middle of the gene. Eraser: KDM4A.
La queue de H4 aide les nucléosomes vois: The H4 tail helps neighbouring nucleosomes come together. One acetyl on its lysine 16 is enough to hinder folding of the fibre (shown on fibres reconstituted in vitro): the chromatin stays open. Writer: MOF (KAT8), in the MSL and NSL complexes. Erasers: the sirtuins SIRT1 and SIRT2, NAD⁺-dependent deacetylases. This mark acts mainly through its physical effect on the fibre.
Un acétyle sur la lysine 27 de H3 neutra: An acetyl on lysine 27 of H3 neutralises its positive charge: this is the mark of active enhancers and promoters. Writers: p300 and CBP (genes EP300 and CREBBP), which take the acetyl from acetyl-CoA. Reader: BRD4, through its bromodomains, which prefers tails acetylated at several positions. Erasers: HDAC1 and HDAC2 (for example in the NuRD complex) and HDAC3. The same lysine cannot be both acetylated and methylated: H3K27ac and H3K27me3 exclude each other.
Un seul méthyle sur la même lysine 4, et: A single methyl on the same lysine 4, and the message changes: where H3K4me3 is scarce, H3K4me1 signals an enhancer, a regulatory region at a distance from the gene. Writers: KMT2C and KMT2D (also called MLL3 and MLL4), which add one or two methyls. Eraser: LSD1 (KDM1A), which decommissions enhancers when a cell differentiates. On its own, this mark designates a waiting enhancer; it becomes active when lysine 27 is acetylated (next step).
Trois méthyles sur la lysine 4 de H3 : l: Three methyls on lysine 4 of H3: the signature of active promoters, around the transcription start site. Writers: mostly SET1A and SET1B, in the COMPASS complex (KMT2A and KMT2B at some genes); the methyl donor is S-adenosylmethionine (SAM). Reader: the PHD finger of TAF3, a subunit of TFIID, which helps to install the transcription machinery. Erasers: the KDM5 demethylases (here KDM5C). This mark also prevents the DNA methyltransferases DNMT3 from binding the H3 tail, which is thought to help keep the CpG islands of active promoters unmethylated.
Un nucléosome, grossi environ un million: A nucleosome, magnified about a million times: 147 base pairs of DNA (grey-blue) make 1.65 turns around eight histones, two copies each of H3 (blue), H4 (green), H2A (yellow) and H2B (pink). Histone H1 sits where the DNA leaves. The histone tails, flexible, stick out: this is mostly where enzymes “write” small chemical marks (methyl, acetyl, phosphate, ubiquitin) on specific residues, which other proteins “read” and yet others “erase”. Each step shows one mark, its writer (blue-green), its reader (violet), its eraser (ochre) and what it means. The colours of the marks are those of chromatin-state maps: red for an active promoter, yellow and orange for an enhancer, green for a transcribed gene, grey for Polycomb, blue-violet for heterochromatin.

Like most promoters, its promoter carries H3K4me3, and its acetylation is constantly renewed; an RNA polymerase II that has already engaged waits there, paused, held by NELF and DSIF (shown in fibroblasts and neuroendocrine cells). The enhancers carry H3K4me1 but not yet H3K27ac. This is what lets the gene start within minutes.

In the gene body, the general pattern of transcribed genes: H3K79me2 then H3K36me3.
Quand le fer manque ou que l'érythropoïé: When iron is scarce or erythropoietin stimulates red cell production, the deacetylase HDAC3 and its partner NCOR1 repress HAMP: H3K9 acetylation and H3K4me3 disappear from the promoter, and transcription drops. This repression is reversible: it is not heterochromatin. Less hepcidin means more iron absorbed by the gut and released into the blood.
Au promoteur, où se fixent les SMAD (voi: At the promoter, where the SMADs (BMP6 pathway) and STAT3 (interleukin 6 pathway) bind: H3K4me3 (red) and acetylated H3K9 (light orange), measured in mouse liver. Elsewhere, the beads follow the general pattern of transcribed genes (H3K27ac and H3K4me1 at the enhancer, H3K79me2 then H3K36me3 in the gene body), which has not been measured on HAMP specifically.
Dans une cellule qui n'exprime pas la β-: In a cell that does not express β-globin (measurements made in HeLa cells), the locus carries neither acetylation nor H3K4 methylation; H3K9 is methylated over a wide stretch (blue-violet), the chromatin resists DNase and replicates late. DNA methylation of the promoter is often high, but varies between tissues. No polymerase travels along the gene.

H3S10ph juste à côté de H3K9me3 : un chr: H3S10ph right next to H3K9me3: a chromosome in mitosis. Aurora B phosphorylates serine 10, and HP1 comes off the neighbouring lysine 9.
H3K9me3, H4K20me3 et ADN méthylé : l'hét: H3K9me3, H4K20me3 and methylated DNA: constitutive heterochromatin, closed in every cell (pericentromeric regions, transposable elements). HP1 reads H3K9me3.
H3K27me3 et H2AK119ub1 : un gène éteint: H3K27me3 and H2AK119ub1: a gene silenced by Polycomb (facultative heterochromatin). PRC2 writes the first mark, PRC1 the second.
H3K4me3 sur une queue de H3, H3K27me3 su: H3K4me3 on one H3 tail, H3K27me3 on the other: a bivalent promoter, silent but ready to start. This state was described in embryonic stem cells, on developmental genes.
H2BK120ub1 et H3K79me2 : le début d'un g: H2BK120ub1 and H3K79me2: the start of a gene being transcribed. Here the ubiquitin is on H2B, not on H2A as in Polycomb chromatin; it stimulates DOT1L, which writes H3K79me2.
H3K36me3 et ADN méthylé : le corps d'un: H3K36me3 and methylated DNA: the body of a transcribed gene. SETD2 travels with RNA polymerase II and writes H3K36me3; DNMT3B reads this mark and methylates the DNA of the gene body.
H3K4me1 seule : un enhancer en attente,: H3K4me1 alone: a poised enhancer, marked but not yet active. It lacks H3K27ac.
H3K4me1 avec H3K27ac : un enhancer actif: H3K4me1 with H3K27ac: an active enhancer. A single methyl on lysine 4, instead of three, tells an enhancer from a promoter; the acetyl on lysine 27 says it is active.
H3K4me3 avec H3K27ac : un promoteur acti: H3K4me3 with H3K27ac: an active promoter. H3K4me3 borders the transcription start site, the acetyl opens the chromatin, and the variant H2A.Z often occupies the nucleosomes flanking that site.
Quel résidu catalytique utilisent BAP1 e: Which catalytic residue do BAP1 and USP22 use?
BAP1 (famille UCH ; complexe PR-DUB, ave: BAP1 (UCH family; PR-DUB complex, with ASXL1, 2 or 3) removes H2AK119ub1; USP22 (USP family; a module of the SAGA complex) removes H2BK120ub1. Both are cysteine proteases: the active-site cysteine attacks the isopeptide bond, then water releases the ubiquitin.
Une désubiquitinase coupe la liaison : l: A deubiquitinase cuts the bond: the histone gets its lysine back, and the ubiquitin, intact, can be used again.
Oui, sur une lysine de l'E3: Yes, on a lysine of the E3
Non : elle passe directement de l'E2 à l: No: it passes directly from the E2 to the lysine
Une E3 à domaine RING porte-t-elle l'ubi: Does a RING-domain E3 carry the ubiquitin before transferring it?
L'ubiquitine a d'abord été activée par E: Ubiquitin was first activated by E1 (one ATP), then loaded onto the cysteine of an E2 (thioester). A RING-domain E3 never carries the ubiquitin: it holds the charged E2 against the nucleosome, and the lysine attacks the thioester directly. An isopeptide bond forms with glycine 76. RNF20/RNF40 write H2BK120ub1; RING1A or RING1B, in PRC1, write H2AK119ub1. A single ubiquitin is not a degradation signal.
Une protéine entière, l'ubiquitine (76 a: A whole protein, ubiquitin (76 amino acids), is grafted onto a lysine. The E3 enzyme presents to the histone a ubiquitin that is already activated, carried by an E2 enzyme.
Une molécule d'eau, activée par deux ion: A water molecule, activated by two metal ions
Qu'est-ce qui attaque le phosphate dans: What attacks the phosphate in the active site of PP1?
PP1 est une métallophosphatase : les deu: PP1 is a metallophosphatase: the two metal ions of its active site activate a water molecule, which attacks the phosphorus. At mitotic exit, Repo-Man brings PP1 onto the chromosomes and H3 is dephosphorylated. γH2AX, for its part, is erased by PP2A and PP4.
Une phosphatase hydrolyse la liaison : l: A phosphatase hydrolyses the bond: the phosphate leaves, and the serine is free again.
Quel phosphate de l'ATP est transféré ?: Which phosphate of ATP is transferred?
En mitose, Aurora B phosphoryle la sérin: In mitosis, Aurora B phosphorylates serine 10 of H3: the serine hydroxyl attacks the γ-phosphate of ATP. Right next to lysine 9, this phosphate drives HP1 off H3K9me3. The same chemistry writes γH2AX: ATM, ATR or DNA-PK phosphorylate serine 139 of H2AX around a double-strand break.
Une kinase transfère le dernier phosphat: A kinase transfers the last phosphate of an ATP onto a serine of histone H3: the tail gains negative charges.
Le phosphate vient de l'ATP et repart pa: The phosphate comes from ATP and leaves by hydrolysis. Ubiquitin arrives already activated, on an E2 enzyme, and leaves intact. These marks respond quickly: γH2AX appears within minutes around a break, H3S10ph covers the chromosomes for the duration of mitosis.
Quatre réactions : un phosphate posé sur: Four reactions: a phosphate put on a serine then removed, a whole ubiquitin grafted onto a lysine then detached.
Que devient le méthyle retiré ?: What becomes of the removed methyl?
Dioxygénases à Fe²⁺ et α-cétoglutarate,: Fe²⁺- and α-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases, like the TETs: the methyl is hydroxylated to an unstable hemiaminal, which releases formaldehyde. Several act on trimethylated lysine: KDM5 on H3K4me3, KDM4 on H3K9me3 and H3K36me3, KDM6 (UTX, JMJD3) on H3K27me3.
Une autre famille de déméthylases hydrox: Another family of demethylases hydroxylates the methyl, which then comes off. Several of its members can remove even the third one.
Son azote n'a plus de doublet libre pour: Its nitrogen has no lone pair left to form the imine
Pourquoi LSD1 ne peut-elle pas déméthyle: Why can LSD1 not demethylate a trimethylated lysine?
Le FAD de LSD1 oxyde la liaison C–N de l: The FAD of LSD1 oxidises the C–N bond of methyl-lysine to an imine; water hydrolyses the imine to lysine and formaldehyde, and O₂ reoxidises the FAD, giving H₂O₂. This requires the nitrogen to keep a lone pair: LSD1 removes one or two methyls (H3K4me1 and me2), never the third.
Un méthyle ne se détache pas tel quel :: A methyl does not simply come off: the demethylase LSD1 oxidises it, and it leaves as formaldehyde.
Déméthylase LSD1 (KDM1A), amine oxydase: LSD1 demethylase (KDM1A), an FAD-dependent amine oxidase
H3K4me3 (SET1/MLL) marque les promoteurs: H3K4me3 (SET1/MLL) marks active promoters, H3K36me3 (SETD2) the body of transcribed genes, H3K27me3 (EZH2, PRC2 complex) and H3K9me3 repressed chromatin. Methylation does not change the charge: it is read by chromodomains and PHD domains. In the active site, a single residue (tyrosine or phenylalanine) decides whether the enzyme can go as far as the third methyl.
Les HDAC de classes I, II et IV sont des: Class I, II and IV HDACs are zinc hydrolases, inhibited by vorinostat and valproic acid. Sirtuins (class III) use NAD⁺ and release nicotinamide and O-acetyl-ADP-ribose.
Acétyle : pris sur l'acétyl-CoA, retiré: Acetyl: taken from acetyl-CoA, removed by hydrolysis. Methyl: taken from SAM, removed by oxidation, as formaldehyde. Writers and erasers depend on metabolites (acetyl-CoA, SAM, α-ketoglutarate, FAD, NAD⁺): this is how chromatin senses the metabolic state of the cell.
Cinq réactions qui écrivent ou effacent: Five reactions that write or erase an acetyl or a methyl on a histone lysine, without touching the DNA sequence.
Quelle enzyme insère la nouvelle cytosin: Which enzyme inserts the new cytosine?
APE1 coupe le brin en 5′ du site abasiqu: APE1 cuts the strand 5′ of the abasic site; DNA polymerase β inserts a dCMP opposite the guanine and removes the deoxyribose phosphate; ligase III, with the scaffold protein XRCC1, seals the strand (at the cost of one ATP, not shown). 5hmC can also be lost without excision: DNMT1 methylates poorly a CpG whose other strand carries 5hmC, and the mark is then diluted at each replication.
La réparation de l'ADN comble le site av: DNA repair fills the site with a new, unmethylated cytosine: the cycle is closed.
Réparation par excision de base (APE1, A: Base excision repair (APE1, DNA polymerase β, XRCC1–ligase III)
Les liaisons hydrogène entre les brins: The hydrogen bonds between the strands
Une liaison phosphodiester du brin: A phosphodiester bond of the strand
La liaison N-glycosidique, entre la base: The N-glycosidic bond, between the base and the sugar
TDG hydrolyse la liaison N-glycosidique: TDG hydrolyses the N-glycosidic bond of 5fC and 5caC, not that of 5hmC or 5mC. The deoxyribose stays in the strand: this is an abasic site.
Une glycosylase détache la base oxydée d: A glycosylase detaches the oxidised base from the DNA backbone: a site without a base is left.
5fC → 5caC. Ces deux bases très oxydées: 5fC → 5caC. These two highly oxidised bases are the ones the glycosylase TDG can excise: they designate the cytosine to be replaced.
Troisième oxydation : l'aldéhyde devient: Third oxidation: the aldehyde becomes an acid. This is 5-carboxylcytosine.
Même chimie, avec un deuxième α-cétoglut: Same chemistry, with a second α-ketoglutarate and a second O₂: 5hmC → 5fC. TETs oxidise 5hmC less well than 5mC: this is one reason why 5hmC is a relatively stable base.
La même enzyme recommence : l'hydroxymét: The same enzyme goes again: the hydroxymethyl becomes an aldehyde. This is 5-formylcytosine.
TET1, TET2 et TET3 sont des dioxygénases: TET1, TET2 and TET3 are Fe²⁺- and α-ketoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases: one atom of O₂ goes onto the methyl, the other onto α-ketoglutarate, which is decarboxylated to succinate. 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) is stable; it is most abundant in neurons. The 2-hydroxyglutarate from mutant IDH, succinate and fumarate inhibit the TETs; vitamin C stimulates them.
Pour effacer la marque, une enzyme TET o: To erase the mark, a TET enzyme first oxidises the methyl to hydroxymethyl: an oxygen atom is inserted into it.
Un groupe méthyle est ajouté sur une cyt: A methyl group is added to a cytosine followed by a guanine (CpG). In a promoter, this mark helps switch the gene off.
Cytosine → 5mC → 5hmC → 5fC → 5caC → sit: Cytosine → 5mC → 5hmC → 5fC → 5caC → abasic site → cytosine. Writing costs one SAM; erasing costs three α-ketoglutarates, three O₂ and a new nucleotide. The mark is also lost without any enzyme, by dilution, when it is not copied after replication.
Six réactions pour poser un méthyle sur: Six reactions to put a methyl on a cytosine, then take it off. The mark is not torn off: it is oxidised step by step, then the whole base is replaced.
Sur le chromosome 11 hérité du père, la: On the chromosome 11 inherited from the father, the imprinting control region (ICR) is methylated (blue dots): CTCF cannot bind it. The enhancers (yellow) reach IGF2, which is expressed (bright); H19 stays silent (dark). IGF2 encodes a fetal growth factor. When this allele loses its methylation, IGF2 is silent on both chromosomes: this is a frequent cause of Silver-Russell syndrome (growth restriction). Another imprinted region: 15q11-q13, involved in Prader-Willi syndrome (loss of the paternal contribution) and Angelman syndrome (loss of the maternal contribution).
Empreinte parentale : pour une centaine: Genomic imprinting: for about a hundred genes in mammals, only one of the two alleles is expressed, depending on the parent it came from. Here, at 11p15.5, on the chromosome 11 inherited from the mother: the imprinting control region (ICR), between IGF2 and H19, is not methylated. CTCF (amber) binds it and insulates IGF2 from the enhancers (yellow), which lie beyond H19: H19 is expressed (bright), IGF2 stays silent (dark). Compare with the other chromosome 11. When this allele wrongly carries the paternal methylation, IGF2 is expressed at a double dose: this is one of the mechanisms of Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome. On this same maternal chromosome, a little further along, CDKN1C is expressed, a brake on cell proliferation.
EZH2 (ou EZH1), EED, SUZ12 et RBBP4 ou R: EZH2 (or EZH1), EED, SUZ12 and RBBP4 or RBBP7: EZH2 puts up to three methyls on lysine 27 of H3. EED reads the mark already in place and stimulates EZH2: H3K27me3 thus spreads from nucleosome to nucleosome, and can be passed from the mother cell to the daughter cells. JARID2 reads H2AK119ub1, the mark of PRC1: the two complexes reinforce each other. In embryonic stem cells, PRC2 marks the “bivalent” promoters of developmental genes, which also carry H3K4me3: silent, but ready to start. On differentiation these domains resolve: activated genes keep H3K4me3 and lose H3K27me3.
Bâti autour de RING1A ou RING1B (RNF2),: Built around RING1A or RING1B (RNF2), which puts a ubiquitin on lysine 119 of H2A, with one of the six PCGF proteins. Canonical PRC1 complexes also contain a CBX protein, whose chromodomain reads H3K27me3, and a PHC protein, whose SAM domain polymerises: this is what gathers PRC1 into foci. Variant PRC1 complexes, with RYBP or YAF2 in place of CBX, write most of H2AK119ub1.
Les protéines Polycomb ne sont pas répar: Polycomb proteins are not spread at random in the nucleus: they concentrate in foci, the Polycomb bodies. Here these foci are placed on the four HOX gene clusters (chromosomes 7, 17, 12 and 2), classical Polycomb targets, silenced wholly or partly depending on the cell type: a schematic placement. The gathering of target genes in such bodies was shown in Drosophila; in the mouse, the four Hox clusters contact each other at a distance in embryonic stem cells. Chromatin: H3K27me3 and H2AK119ub1.
Le centromère n'est pas défini par une s: The centromere is defined not by a sequence but by a histone: CENP-A, a variant of H3, replaces H3 there in nucleosomes sitting on α-satellite DNA made of 171-bp repeats. The kinetochore, which attaches the chromosome to the spindle in mitosis, assembles at this place. At replication, the existing CENP-A is shared between the two chromatids; the stock is topped up only in G1, by the chaperone HJURP. The mark is thus passed on without going through the DNA sequence: this is epigenetic inheritance.
Trois protéines voisines chez les mammif: Three related proteins in mammals: HP1α (CBX5), HP1β (CBX1) and HP1γ (CBX3). Their chromodomain recognises H3K9me3; their chromoshadow domain pairs them into dimers, which can bridge two nucleosomes. HP1 also binds SUV39H1, which writes H3K9me3: the mark can thus spread step by step. Nothing here is static: most HP1 molecules exchange within seconds. HP1α can form droplets by phase separation, which may help to set heterochromatin apart.
De part et d'autre de chaque centromère,: On either side of each centromere, megabases of repeated satellite DNA stay compact in every cell: this is constitutive heterochromatin. Its nucleosomes carry H3K9me3 (written by SUV39H1 and SUV39H2), read by HP1, then H4K20me3; its DNA is methylated, and it replicates late in S phase. When the DNA of these satellites loses its methylation, chromosomes 1, 9 and 16 rearrange at this place: this is ICF syndrome.
Une protéine à onze doigts de zinc, qui: A protein with eleven zinc fingers, which recognises an oriented DNA motif. It stops cohesin: at the two feet of a loop, more than nine times out of ten, the two CTCF motifs face each other (convergent orientation). CTCF thus delimits domains (TADs): an enhancer acts on the promoters of its own domain, little on those of the next one. If a chromosomal rearrangement removes or moves a boundary, an enhancer activates the wrong gene: this is the cause of some limb malformations. CTCF does not bind a motif whose DNA is methylated: this is the principle of imprinting at the H19/IGF2 locus.
Un anneau fait de SMC1A, SMC3 et RAD21,: A ring made of SMC1A, SMC3 and RAD21, with STAG1 or STAG2; NIPBL loads it onto DNA. Cohesin extrudes DNA into a loop, using ATP: in vitro, up to 2 kb per second. The loop grows until the ring runs into two CTCF proteins; WAPL then releases it. The human genome thus has about 10,000 loops, and domains (TADs) of the order of a megabase, within which enhancers and promoters meet. When cohesin is destroyed, these loops disappear. The same cohesin holds sister chromatids together until mitosis. Here the ring encircles the DNA of the enhancer and that of the promoter: a schematic drawing.
Un moteur à ATP d'une quinzaine de sous-: An ATP-driven motor of about fifteen subunits, built around one of two ATPases, BRG1 (SMARCA4) or BRM (SMARCA2). It grips a nucleosome and slides the DNA over the octamer, or ejects the octamer: promoters and enhancers become accessible to transcription factors. It opposes Polycomb, which it evicts from chromatin. The genes of its subunits are mutated in about 20% of human cancers; their germline variants cause Coffin-Siris syndrome.
H3.3 ne diffère de H3.1 que par cinq aci: H3.3 differs from H3.1 by only five amino acids (four for H3.2), but it is made throughout the cell cycle and deposited outside replication: by the chaperone HIRA at genes, by the ATRX–DAXX complex at telomeres and pericentromeric heterochromatin. It thus marks active chromatin. Here: turquoise spheres, in place of the blue H3. Another H3 variant: CENP-A, the one at centromeres.
Un variant de H2A, codé par ses propres: A variant of H2A, encoded by its own genes and deposited outside replication: the SRCAP complex exchanges an H2A–H2B dimer for an H2A.Z–H2B dimer. H2A.Z is concentrated in the nucleosomes flanking the transcription start site, and at enhancers. Here: orange spheres, in place of the yellow H2A. Other H2A variants exist: H2AX, whose phosphorylated tail (γH2AX) signals DNA breaks, and macroH2A, concentrated on the inactive X chromosome.
Posée sur le nucléosome à l'endroit où l: Sitting on the nucleosome where the DNA enters and exits, H1 protects about twenty more base pairs (chromatosome, ≈ 168 bp) and draws the two linker strands together: the fibre compacts. It is not fixed: in a living cell each molecule stays in place only a few minutes, then another takes over. Mammals have eleven variants, seven of them somatic. It is rarer on active promoters: here, the nucleosomes next to the promoter carry none.
Surface de la cellule : le bouton « ⇲ Vo: Cell surface: the “⇲ Ways in” button offers several ways to enter and shows the receptors.
La membrane ne laisse passer ni les ions: The membrane lets through neither ions nor large molecules: to get in, you have to be carried in by it. Several routes exist; each has its machinery, its size and its speed. Choose yours: the clathrin route is flown, the others are shown at nanometre scale and then drop you inside the cell.
Les protéines occupent au moins un quart: Proteins occupy at least a quarter of the surface of a plasma membrane (measured on the red cell). Each cell type has its own repertoire of receptors: it decides which signals the cell hears and what it lets in. The shapes drawn are schematic, the sizes realistic.
Au bouton synaptique, la membrane ajouté: At the synaptic bouton, the membrane added by exocytosis is taken back in 50 to 100 milliseconds, without clathrin; clathrin is used only afterwards, to remake vesicles from the endosome. Other, slower routes coexist, depending on how intense the activity is. The ship is in the bouton: it can go on toward the soma.
Chez le neurone, elle a été décrite dans: In neurons, it has been described in growth cones and axons.
Dans l'hépatocyte, elle est montrée à ti: In the hepatocyte, it is shown for comparison: its uptake relies mostly on receptors.
Dans un érythroblaste, cette voie est mo: In an erythroblast, this route is shown for comparison: its iron comes in through the transferrin receptor.
La macropinocytose ne choisit pas : elle: Macropinocytosis does not choose: it swallows the surroundings in micrometre-sized gulps. It serves to feed, to survey the surroundings, to renew the membrane.
Beaucoup de neurones expriment des cavéo: Many neurons express caveolins without forming recognisable caveolae: this route is shown here for comparison.
Des cavéoles ont été décrites sur l'hépa: Caveolae have been described on rat hepatocytes; they are far rarer there than on the neighbouring endothelium.
Dans un érythroblaste, cette voie est mo: In an erythroblast, this route is shown for comparison.
Les cavéoles sont d'abord un organe de l: Caveolae are first of all an organ of the membrane: a reserve of surface, a tension sensor, a signalling platform. Only a small share pinch off and enter.
mGluR2 se tient sur le bouton, hors de l: mGluR2 sits on the bouton, outside the active zone: it gauges the glutamate spilling out of the cleft. It is a G-protein-coupled receptor of a particular kind: it works as a dimer, and each half carries a large outer “flytrap” domain that closes on glutamate. The two helix bundles move closer and activate a Gi/o protein: the bouton releases less glutamate. The neuron brakes itself.
À la zone active du bouton. Sa grande so: At the active zone of the bouton. Its large α1 subunit forms the pore, with four voltage-sensing domains; α2δ protrudes outside, β sits in the cytosol. When the action potential depolarises the membrane, the pore opens: calcium enters and triggers the fusion of synaptic vesicles, a few tens of nanometres away.
Le BDNF, une neurotrophine en dimère, ra: BDNF, a dimeric neurotrophin, brings two TrkB receptors together. Their kinases phosphorylate each other and start three pathways: Ras–ERK, PI3K–Akt and PLCγ. The active complex is internalised by a clathrin-coated pit and travels to the soma in a signalling endosome: this is the main way into this neuron.
Presque propre à l'hépatocyte, qui en po: Almost exclusive to the hepatocyte, which carries hundreds of thousands of them. Its heads are lectins: they recognise the galactose (yellow) exposed at the tip of the sugars of a plasma glycoprotein once it has lost its sialic acids. The protein is internalised by a clathrin-coated pit and destroyed. RNA-interference drugs fitted with three N-acetylgalactosamines use this receptor to enter the liver only.
À jeun, le glucagon donne l'ordre invers: During fasting, glucagon gives the opposite order. Its receptor crosses the membrane seven times: it is a G-protein-coupled receptor. The hormone slips between the outer domain and the helices; the receptor then activates the Gs protein, whose α subunit goes off to stimulate adenylyl cyclase. Cyclic AMP (yellow) activates protein kinase A: glycogen is broken down and glucose returned to the blood.
Deux chaînes α et deux chaînes β, soudée: Two α chains and two β chains, joined by disulfide bridges. Without insulin its outer part draws an inverted V, feet apart: the two kinases, in the cytosol, are too far from each other. Insulin tips it into a T: the feet come together, the kinases phosphorylate each other, then phosphorylate the IRS proteins. Through PI3-kinase and Akt, the hepatocyte then stores glucose as glycogen.
Une LDL est une particule de 22 nm : un: An LDL is a 22-nm particle: a core of cholesteryl esters, belted by a single apolipoprotein B-100. The receptor grasps it with its seven cysteine-rich repeats. The complex is internalised by a clathrin-coated pit; in the endosome, acidity makes the receptor let go, and it returns to the surface. Its variants cause familial hypercholesterolaemia.
Les intégrines attachent la cellule à se: Integrins attach the cell to its neighbours and to the matrix. At rest the integrin is folded over on itself and binds its ligand poorly. When talin (ochre) binds its tail, on the cytosolic side, it unfolds like a switchblade to nearly 20 nm and grasps its ligand: here VCAM-1, carried by the macrophage at the centre of the erythroblastic island.
KIT est un récepteur à activité tyrosine: KIT is a receptor tyrosine kinase: five immunoglobulin domains outside, a kinase inside. Stem cell factor (SCF), a dimer, brings two KIT together; their kinases phosphorylate each other and the signal goes out. It supports the survival and multiplication of erythroid precursors, alongside EPO.
Sans ce signal, l'érythroblaste meurt. L: Without this signal the erythroblast dies. The EPO receptor is a preformed dimer, each chain carrying a JAK2 kinase (ochre) on the cytosolic side. EPO, a hormone made by the kidney when oxygen is short, lodges between the two chains and reorients them: the two JAK2 phosphorylate each other (yellow grains), then phosphorylate STAT5 (violet), which leaves for the nucleus to switch on survival and differentiation genes.
Le récepteur de la transferrine est un d: The transferrin receptor is a butterfly-shaped dimer. Each wing binds one transferrin, a two-lobed protein carrying two Fe³⁺ ions (red). The erythroblast displays several hundred thousand of them: it needs iron for the haem of its haemoglobin. The complex is internalised by a clathrin-coated pit: this is the main way into this cell.
En quelques secondes, la clathrine (roug: Within a few seconds, clathrin (dark red) buds 40-nm vesicles from the endosome. Once uncoated, they are filled with glutamate by the transporter VGLUT, powered by the proton pump V-ATPase, then rejoin the reserve, ready for another cycle. Here clathrin serves to remake vesicles, not to take the membrane back.
En une seconde environ, la grande vésicu: In about a second, the large vesicle fuses with an endosome of the bouton. The ship is inside the neuron; the membrane, for its part, will be cut back to the right size.
La membrane est reprise aussitôt, au bor: The membrane is taken back at once, at the edge of the active zone, by a pit much wider than a synaptic vesicle, which gives a single large vesicle. No clathrin coat: it takes actin (orange) and dynamin (blue-green), which cuts the neck. This is ultrafast endocytosis; the ship takes the ride.
Un potentiel d'action arrive. Les canaux: An action potential arrives. Cav2.1 calcium channels (blue-green) open, calcium enters, and a docked vesicle fuses with the membrane in under a millisecond. It is about 40 nm across and releases its glutamate (yellow) into the cleft, 20 nm wide, as far as the receptors opposite. Its membrane is added to that of the bouton: it has to be taken back.
Le macropinosome s'enfonce dans la cellu: The macropinosome sinks into the cell, loses water and shrinks. Tubules send its membrane back to the surface; its lumen acidifies, Rab5 gives way to Rab7, then it fuses with lysosomes, where its contents are digested. Cancer cells with mutant Ras feed in this way on albumin from their surroundings; viruses such as vaccinia enter by this route.
Les bords du repli se rejoignent et fusi: The edges of the fold meet and fuse: the gulp is enclosed in a macropinosome more than 0.2 µm across, far larger than a clathrin-coated vesicle. Amiloride and its derivatives block this route. Macrophages and dendritic cells do it all the time, to sample their surroundings; other cells mostly when a growth factor prompts them.
Poussée par l'actine, la membrane se dre: Pushed by actin, the membrane rears up into a circular fold nearly a micrometre high: a cup open to the outside. No receptor sorts what lies in it: the cell is about to swallow a gulp of the surrounding fluid, with everything it contains.
Ici l'échelle change : le micromètre. Un: Here the scale changes: the micrometre. A growth factor such as EGF (orange) binds its receptor. Through Ras and PI3-kinase, the signal activates the small GTPase Rac1, which makes actin polymerise (orange filaments) under the membrane, in a circle more than a micrometre across. Proteins are drawn enlarged so they stay visible.
La plupart des cavéoles restent à la sur: Most caveolae stay at the surface. Some pinch off: EHD2 leaves the neck, dynamin (blue-green) constricts it, and the vesicle, still wearing its coat, reaches an early endosome and fuses with it. The cargo is sorted; caveolins and cavins can return to the surface.
Scission et trajet vers l'endosome: Scission and the trip to the endosome
Une propriété que n'ont pas les puits à: A property clathrin-coated pits do not have: when the membrane is stretched (cell swelling, a stretched muscle), the caveola unfolds within moments and gives its surface back to the membrane, which does not tear. The cavins come off; the caveolins stay in the membrane. When tension drops, the caveola forms again. It is a membrane reserve as much as a way in.
Le col reste ouvert : ce qui baigne la c: The neck stays open: whatever bathes the cell gets in, such as plasma albumin (pale spheres). The ship slips into the caveola.
Une petite outre de 50 à 80 nm, ouverte: A small flask 50 to 80 nm across, open to the outside. Its coat is made of caveolin-1 (gold), whose disc-shaped oligomers are embedded in the inner leaflet of the membrane, and of cavins (violet), which sheathe it with filaments. EHD2 (green) sits at the neck and holds it at the surface. The membrane here is rich in cholesterol and sphingolipids. Caveolae abound in endothelium, adipocytes and muscle cells.
Sept parcours. Le premier présente les c: Seven tours. The first presents the cells of the brain, at micrometre scale. The other six follow a signal through a region of the brain, then on to its effects in the body. In each view: drag to orbit around the scene, wheel or pinch to zoom.
L'hypothalamus et le tronc cérébral tien: The hypothalamus and brainstem keep the body within narrow limits, through nerves and hormones, without our having to think about it.
Soif, eau, respiration : quatre étapes s: Thirst, water, breathing: four steps on settings that do not go through consciousness.
Très vite par les nerfs, plus lentement: Very fast through nerves, more slowly through hormones, the brain readies the whole body to cope; then cortisol closes the loop. The hepatocyte's glucagon and insulin receptors can be seen in “⇲ Ways in”, in front of the hepatocyte.
Une alarme dans l'amygdale, deux voies v: An alarm in the amygdala, two routes to the body, and a brake: six steps, as far as the heart and the liver.
Décider n'est pas l'affaire d'une seule: Deciding is not the business of a single region: the frontal cortex proposes and holds back, dopamine learns what is worthwhile, the basal ganglia settle it. The output is a movement — or its absence.
Cortex préfrontal, dopamine et noyaux gr: Prefrontal cortex, dopamine and basal ganglia: five steps on what makes us choose one action and hold back the others.
Apprendre, c'est changer la force de syn: Learning means changing the strength of synapses, then the structure of circuits. The body takes part: sleep, stress hormones, emotions.
De l'hippocampe au cortex, et du corps à: From hippocampus to cortex, and from body to hippocampus: five steps.
Un geste simple mobilise le cortex, les: A simple movement calls on the cortex, the basal ganglia, the brainstem, the spinal cord, the nerve, the muscle and the cerebellum. The synapse between neurons can be visited in this game: the “⚡ Follow a nerve impulse” button, inside the neuron.
De l'intention à la contraction d'un mus: From intention to the contraction of a muscle, then to its correction: six steps, from the frontal cortex to the hand.
La vision n'est pas une image projetée d: Vision is not an image projected into the brain: it is an analysis in stages, from retina to cortex, with several outputs to the body, which set the pupil, the gaze, the reaching hand and the clock.
De la lumière au cortex, puis du cortex: From light to cortex, then from cortex to body: six steps on a model of the brain. The right hemisphere is seen from its inner face; pathways are correct in their relays, schematic in their course.
Le cerveau n'est pas fait que de neurone: The brain is not made of neurons alone, and neurons are not alike: each shape is the tool of a function. In adults, the addition of new neurons in the hippocampus, clear in rodents, is still debated in humans.
Huit étapes à l'échelle du micromètre :: Eight steps at micrometre scale: the main types of neurons, then the cells that surround, feed and defend them. Shapes are drawn after their real look, by random generation: no neuron has exactly this shape.
Les capillaires du cerveau sont étanches: Brain capillaries are sealed: their endothelial cells are joined by tight junctions (yellow), including claudin-5; pericytes (orange) and astrocyte endfeet (green) surround them. This is the blood–brain barrier. The ventricles, for their part, are lined with ciliated ependymal cells. Cerebrospinal fluid, about 500 mL a day, comes mostly from the choroid plexuses.
Ce sont les cellules immunitaires du cer: These are the immune cells of the brain. They do not come from the bone marrow: their precursors settle very early in the embryo. At rest, their processes never stop extending and retracting to inspect the tissue. During development they remove synapses, with the help of complement. Their share ranges from 0.5 to 16.6% of cells depending on the region of the human brain.
Un oligodendrocyte enroule sa membrane a: An oligodendrocyte wraps its membrane around segments of many axons, up to about fifty: this is myelin, an insulator. Between two sheaths, at the nodes of Ranvier, the axon is bare and concentrates its Nav1.6 sodium channels (yellow): the action potential jumps from node to node, far faster than it would creep.
Chaque astrocyte occupe son propre terri: Each astrocyte occupies its own territory, which it fills with very fine processes: in rodents it touches of the order of 100,000 synapses there. The human astrocyte is 2.6 times wider and bears ten times more main processes. Its endfeet cover the capillaries; it takes up the glutamate released at synapses through its transporters GLT-1 and GLAST, and keeps a reserve of glycogen.
Environ 95 % des neurones du striatum (m: About 95% of striatal neurons (measured in the mouse) are medium spiny neurons, GABAergic, with dendrites covered in spines: some carry the D1 dopamine receptor, others the D2. They bathe in the terminals of the dopamine neurons of the substantia nigra, whose axon branches to an extreme: in the rat, a single one covers on average 2.7% of the striatum.
La cellule de Purkinje déploie son arbre: The Purkinje cell spreads its dendritic tree in a single plane, like a trained fruit tree. It is the only output of the cerebellar cortex, and it is inhibitory. It receives a single climbing fibre (orange), which winds around its dendrites, and of the order of 175,000 parallel-fibre synapses (measured in the rat), crossing the tree at right angles. These fibres are the axons of granule cells, the most numerous neurons of the brain, which have only four short dendrites.
Le cervelet : Purkinje et grains: The cerebellum: Purkinje and granule cells
Entre 12 et 25 % des neurones du cortex: Between 12 and 25% of cortical neurons release GABA and restrain their neighbours. Three main families: parvalbumin cells (green), among them the fast basket cells that clasp the body of the pyramidal neuron; somatostatin cells (orange), whose axon climbs to restrain the distant dendrites; VIP cells (violet), which inhibit other interneurons and so release the brake. Chandelier cells (light blue) target the axon initial segment, where the action potential is born.
Le cerveau humain compte environ 86 mill: The human brain has about 86 billion neurons and about as many other cells; the cerebral cortex holds about 16 billion of them. Most of its neurons are pyramidal: a pyramid-shaped cell body, a long dendrite rising toward the surface, a tuft of dendrites at the base, and an axon that carries the message far away and releases glutamate. A human pyramidal neuron of the superficial layers receives of the order of 30,000 excitatory synapses. This is the neuron you visit in this game.
D'autres réglages ne passent jamais par: Other settings never reach consciousness. In the medulla, the preBötzinger complex is thought to generate the rhythm of inspiration (shown in the newborn rat). The order descends to the motoneurons of the phrenic nerve, between the third and fifth cervical vertebrae, and the diaphragm contracts, some fifteen times a minute, for a lifetime.
Dans le rein, la vasopressine se fixe au: In the kidney, vasopressin binds the V2 receptor of collecting-duct cells. Cyclic AMP and protein kinase A insert water channels, aquaporin-2, into the membrane facing the urine: water returns to the blood and the urine becomes concentrated.
Effet dans le corps : le rein retient l': Effect in the body: the kidney retains water
Ces neurones magnocellulaires, dans les: These magnocellular neurons, in the supraoptic and paraventricular nuclei, send their axons down to the posterior pituitary. There their action potentials release vasopressin straight into the blood: a neuron that secretes a hormone.
Vous avez transpiré : le sang se concent: You have been sweating: the blood becomes more concentrated. After damage to this region, intelligence is intact but decisions become disastrous. The case of Phineas Gage, whose skull was pierced by an iron bar in 1848, is the famous illustration: he survived, but his character changed.
